neighbours.label: ' it' as the subject of a main or subordinate clause right after a connective or an introductory clause ('When X, it ...', 'Instead, it ...', 'because it ...'), vs 'it' as an object or sentence-initial 'It'
fire: The storm moved east overnight. When the wind dropped, it left a calm sea behind.
The board rejected the merger. Instead, it voted to sell two smaller units.
Our old printer was replaced because it kept jamming on thick paper.
The drug is cheap to make. However, it must be stored at low temperature.
As the river rose, it flooded the lower fields within hours.
The museum closed in March. Later, it reopened with a new wing.
The bridge was rebuilt since it could no longer carry heavy lorries.
The company grew quickly. By 2010, it employed over two thousand people.
quiet: The storm moved east overnight, and the fishermen watched it from the harbour.
The board read the merger offer and quickly rejected it on Monday.
Our old printer kept jamming, so we finally gave it away.
The drug is cheap to make. It must be stored at low temperature.
The river rose all night, and the farmers could only watch it.
The museum closed in March. It reopened with a new wing.
The old bridge was weak, so the council rebuilt it last year.
The company grew quickly. It employed over two thousand people.

predictions: Subject ' it' after a connective reaches 0.35-0.5; object 'it' and initial 'It' stay under 0.15.
notes: Card: tiny-max (0.21) broad pole; 12 of the top 32 peak on ' it' after a comma ('With this, it', 'Instead, it'). Probe: 'When prices rise, it' 0.430, 'Instead, it' 0.490, 'because it was' 0.383, but 'With this in mind, it' only 0.152; object 'put it on' 0.130, sentence-initial 'It is' 0.097; 'Int|roducing' 0.502 (a second trigger, not tested here).
